- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is low, model underestimates future price spikes — increase forecast by 15–30% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is high, model overestimates downside — reduce forecast by 20–40% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 3x recent mean), model often overreacts with excessive overshoot — cap forecast at 2x prior peak or 1.5x true spike for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is erratic, model lacks momentum — smooth forecast using 3-day moving average of history.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underpredict mean reversion — add 10–20% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., -0.67 → 1.00), model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 10–25% for next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by > 50% in 3–5 days, model is “overly conservative” — increase forecast by 20–30% for next 3–5 days, especially if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is consistently positive and forecast is consistently low, model is “missing sentiment momentum” — add 10–20% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
